priceRoutes.route: (one resource, served over 402-style challenge/settle, not an HTTP framework route in this package)
priceRoutes.price: resource.price in HBD, e.g. "0.002" (Hive-Backed Dollars), not USD/USDC

reasonsNotFoldable: This is not an x402/USDC seller under market.561.group's rails at all: it settles in HBD over the Hive blockchain's own memo-transfer convention (a 'hbd-transfer-scheme', per its own package description), not the x402 'exact' EVM scheme on Base that the kernel's offer.mjs and priceAtomicUnits (USDC, six decimals) are built for. There is no USD-to-USDC-atomic conversion to replace here; the pricing unit itself is foreign to the kernel's price grammar (offer.schema.json's price field is a US-dollar string, not an HBD string).

sellHiveExitTightnessResource's core verification step (verifyHbdPayment) makes its own live reads against two caller-supplied public Hive nodes to independently confirm a claimed transfer - a live network verification against a rail the market kernel's facilitator/settlement model has no concept of (there is no Hive facilitator abstraction anywhere in x402-services-section).

On a verified payment it calls settleHbdPurchase (its own settlement/journal computation, distinct from the kernel's settlementWitness) and then invokes an external report command as a child process (execute-javascript-node-command-service, wired in apps/x402-hive-exit-tightness-seller-cli.mjs to run the aagaard hive-engine-exit-tightness.mjs probe as `node <script> --account <a> --symbol <s>`) - a live subprocess invocation, not a value-returning pure function of the request body/query, which the compute binding cannot express.

The seller-cli additionally writes durable settlement-witness journal state via @red-cup-engineering/semantic-record-journal-service when journalRoot is supplied - another live/durable side effect outside the binding model.
whatTheMarketEngineWouldNeed: A second settlement rail entirely - a Hive HBD memo-transfer scheme alongside the market's current EVM 'exact' scheme, including its own challenge/verify/settle vocabulary distinct from x402's payment-required/payment-signature headers.

A price grammar that admits non-USD, non-USDC settlement units (or a documented USD-equivalent conversion the founder is willing to authorize, at which point priceAtomicUnits still would not apply since the settlement asset is HBD, not USDC).

A compute-binding extension that can invoke an external command (not just an imported pure function) for the report-production step, or a rewrite of the aagaard probe into an importable pure function - either is real engineering work, not a catalog entry.
